card: Caps the -maxconnections setting at 2,000 automatic connections, warning users and clamping higher values during node initialization. Previously, the option had no upper bound, exposing nodes with unusually high connection limits to an assertion crash in the transaction orphanage when peer counts exceed 3,000. Capping happens before reserving file descriptors and uses saturating integer parsing to prevent integer overflow on large argument inputs.
changed_since_previous: Switched from modifying TxOrphanage trimming logic and DoS score bounds to clamping the -maxconnections configuration setting at 2,000 in node initialization.
evidence: PR description: 'The orphanage can abort when more than 3,000 peers have orphan announcements. The -maxconnections setting currently has no explicit upper bound.'
Commit message: 'Limit the configurable automatic peer count to 2000, leaving headroom below the default orphanage latency limit.'
problem: The -maxconnections setting previously had no upper bound. Nodes configured with very high connection counts risk crashing in the transaction orphanage, which aborts when peer counts exceed 3,000 during orphan announcement trimming.

risk.why: Faulty clamping could prevent operators running specialized high-connection nodes from accepting desired peer counts.

summary: Caps the -maxconnections configuration setting at 2,000 automatic peer connections during node initialization. If a user specifies a higher value, the setting is clamped and an initialization warning is emitted before reserving file descriptors. Large command-line inputs are parsed using saturating integer conversion to prevent integer overflow.
